_provenance.note: tgId 1, tcId 25 — a largest-macLen case (160 bits / 20 bytes) whose key is 121 bytes. Independently re-verified against Python's hmac (OpenSSL-equivalent) oracle before use: HMAC-SHA-384 truncated to 20 bytes reproduces the stated mac exactly. Replaces a self-generated (Node-oracle) vector. See hmac_test.json's note on why this uses CKM_SHA384_HMAC_GENERAL (hsm_hmacVerifyGeneral) rather than the exact-length-only CKM_SHA384_HMAC — same reasoning applies to every width. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the hub's copy of this file, which uses tcId 5: that case's key is only 26 bytes, and this engine enforces a 48-byte minimum for SHA-384-HMAC keys (kMacMechTable minKeyBytes in SoftHSM_sign.cpp), stricter than PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.23.3's suggested FIPS-198 floor of 24. 33 of this group's 150 cases carry sub-48-byte keys; tcId 25 is the same macLen the hub selected for, from the same NIST file and release, with a key this token accepts.
